title_hint: User interview with a consultant about how she writes up client calls
user_notes:
- dana consultant, 5 calls/day
- 20 min writeup each
- bot = dealbreaker, local only
- wants action items, no halluc names
- would pay 10-12/mo
- beta link in 3wks

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Thanks for doing this, Dana. Is it okay if I take notes on my laptop while we talk?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Sure, go ahead. Just, um, I'm not saying anything confidential, right?

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: No, just how you handle meetings. Walk me through your last client call, what did you do afterwards?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: So, I usually scribble in a notebook, then, uh, after the call I type it up in, like, Notion, which takes forever.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: How long?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Twenty minutes per call, maybe more. I do like five calls a day so, yeah, it adds up.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Have you tried any of the AI note tools?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: I tried a couple, the ones that join as a bot. My clients hated it. One literally asked me to leave the bot out.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: So the bot in the call is a dealbreaker.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: For me, yes. Anything that, that sends audio to some cloud, I can't, my clients are in, er, regulated industries.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: If everything stayed on your laptop, would that change it?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Totally. That's the thing that would make me, make me switch honestly.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: What about the notes quality, what do you care about most?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Action items. Who does what by when. And, um, not hallucinating names. It turned my client's name Dubois into Dubai once, which was hilarious but, no.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Ha. Do you want to edit the notes after?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Yes, I'd edit everything. But a good first draft saves me the twenty minutes.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Pricing thoughts? Would you pay for it?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Um, if it's local, I'd pay like ten, twelve euros a month. Not twenty.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Good to know. I'm hoping to have a beta build ready in about three weeks. I'll send you the link when it's ready.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Please do. I'll try it on a real call the following week and tell you what breaks.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Great, that would be super helpful. It supports French too, but accuracy there is still so-so.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Oh yeah, half my calls are in French. And I'd probably want a Notion export someday.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Noted. Anything I forgot to ask?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: No. Maybe ask the next person whether they'd pay yearly. Anyway, good luck.

action_items.task: Send Dana the beta build link when ready (about three weeks)
Try the beta on a real call the week after and report what breaks

non_action_traps: Suggestion to ask the next interviewee about yearly pricing (suggestion, not a commitment)
